## Claims
- [source-backed] The supplied synopsis records the conjecture that both Schur generating sets are minimal, with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 12-33]
- [proved] Assume the standard box model \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(q=n-r\), and \(J_v=\bigoplus_{\mu\supseteq i^j}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). If \(i=1\), put \(a=\min(q-1,r-j)\). Then
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline e_{j+t}.
  \]
  Consequently both families
  \[
  \{s_{(t+1,1^{j-1})}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad
  \{s_{(1^{j+t})}:0\le t\le a\}
  \]
  map to integral bases and are irredundant generators of \(J_v\).
- [proved] If \(j=1\), put \(a=\min(q-i,r-1)\). Then
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_{i+t},
  \]
  and both families
  \[
  \{s_{(i+t)}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad
  \{s_{(i,1^t)}:0\le t\le a\}
  \]
  map to integral bases and are irredundant.

## Strategy
For \(i=1\), dual Jacobi--Trudi shows
\[
J_v=(e_j,e_{j+1},\ldots,e_r)\subseteq A.
\]
Indeed, every \(s_\mu\) with \(\ell(\mu)\ge j\) expands along the first row of its dual Jacobi--Trudi determinant into terms divisible by some \(e_k\), \(k\ge j\).

Write \(P=\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]\). The recurrence from \(E(-t)H(t)=1\) is
\[
e_n=\sum_{k=1}^{q}(-1)^{k-1}h_ke_{n-k}\qquad(n>q).
\]
Hence \(e_n\in P_+(e_j,\ldots,e_{n-1})\) for \(n\ge j+q\). Thus only
\[
e_j,e_{j+1},\ldots,e_{\min(r,j+q-1)}
\]
can survive modulo \(A_+J_v\), giving \(a+1\) candidates.

Their independence follows from the consecutive-elementary complete-intersection presentation
\[
P/(e_j,e_{j+1},\ldots,e_{j+q-1}),
\]
the box presentation for the \((j-1)\times q\) Grassmannian. Over \(\mathbb Q\), its \(q\) defining elements form a regular sequence; therefore \(e_{j+t}\notin(e_j,\ldots,e_{j+t-1})\). Since all candidates have degree at most \(r\), the box relations \(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}\) cannot create a relation in their degrees. Distinct degrees then give an integral free basis.

Dual Jacobi--Trudi for the hook gives
\[
s_{(t+1,1^{j-1})}\equiv (-1)^t e_{j+t}\pmod {A_+J_v}.
\]
The column family is exactly \(s_{(1^{j+t})}=e_{j+t}\). This proves the \(i=1\) assertion.

For \(j=1\), apply the involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), which identifies the \(q^r\)-box quotient with the \(r^q\)-box quotient and exchanges \(e_k\) with \(h_k\). It carries the \(i=1\) result in the transposed box to the stated \(j=1\) result.

## Gaps
- The proof uses the standard integral box presentation and Schur-basis freeness of the Grassmannian quotient; these hypotheses should be independently checked in the formal compilation.
- The consecutive-elementary regular-sequence step is the main commutative-algebra point requiring reviewer verification.
- No statement is made here for \(b>1\).
